title: Volume 10 · Migration: Mapping, Opening Balances and Import
subtitle: Lessons 1–4: a mapping workbook the client signs, masters imported in dependency order, and an opening trial balance that balances to the cent
outcomes: Build a mapping workbook before anything is imported
Import masters in the order the system demands, not the order of the spreadsheet
Load opening balances so the trial balance balances first time
Freeze the opening and prove it with evidence the auditor accepts

slides.title: Build the mapping workbook before you touch the system
bullets: Mapping is a written agreement: old value, new value, owner, decision date
Chart of accounts mapping is the hardest part, because old codes carry history and habit
Every unmapped value is a future support ticket, so count them down to zero
The client signs the workbook, which is what ends the argument in month two

rows: Chart of accounts, customers, suppliers, items
Sheet per entity with old and new columns
Old 1100 Debtors to Debtors - SM, and so on
Codes with no obvious target flagged in red
Workbook v1 approved on a date

slides.notes: The workbook is the deliverable that separates a migration from an improvisation, and its most valuable column is the owner. Every red row needs a name beside it, because the client's finance manager will otherwise assume you decided. Sign one version, date it, and treat later changes as change requests with a cost.

slides.title: Prove the workbook is complete before import
bullets: Completeness means every old value has a target, including the ones nobody uses
Duplicates must be merged before import, not after, because merged history is messy
Tax categories, territories and price lists are the fields people forget
A trial import into a test company is cheaper than a second migration
slides.notes: Thirty eight of thirty eight sounds trivial until the client's chart has one dormant account used once in 2019, and that is exactly the row an auditor finds. Run the trial import into a test company, fix errors there, and keep the log as evidence. The test company costs an hour; a re-migration costs a weekend and the client's confidence.

slides.title: Import in dependency order, not spreadsheet order
bullets: ERPNext needs parents before children: item groups before items, territories before customers
Import small batches and check the log after each, rather than one giant file
Use the template download for each doctype, because column names must match exactly
Never import a field the business does not use, because unused data becomes noise

rows: 5 customers with credit limits and tax category

slides.notes: Dependency order is the rule people break first, usually by importing items before item groups and then wondering why every row fails. Import five records, read the log, then continue. That rhythm feels slow for the first ten minutes and saves hours later, because the first error tells you the column name is wrong before five hundred rows are queued.

slides.title: Rows, errors and duplicates, counted
bullets: The import log is the evidence: rows attempted, created, updated and failed
A successful import of the wrong data is worse than a failed one, so spot-check content
Duplicates usually come from trailing spaces in names, which the system treats as distinct
Re-run the import after fixing errors, using update mode rather than creating again

rows: Search by name and by abbreviation

slides.notes: Counting rows is the easy half; spot-checking content is the half that matters. Open three records at random and read the fields the business depends on: valuation, tax template, warehouse. If those are right, the rest of the row probably is too. If they are wrong, the column mapping is off by one and the whole file needs re-running.

slides.title: Load an opening trial balance that balances
bullets: Opening balances are a journal dated the day before go-live, not a set of typed invoices
Debtors and creditors open as party balances so ageing starts on day one
Stock opens at valuation through a stock reconciliation, not through the journal
Equity is the plug that makes it balance, and the client must agree the figure

rows: Journal to Debtors - SM with party rows, 13,200.00

slides.notes: The arithmetic is the deliverable: 5,640 plus 13,200 plus 18,450 plus 59,000 of fixed assets is 96,290 of assets, against 1,188 plus 1,080 plus 800 of liabilities and 93,222 of equity. Make the learner write both sides before saving the journal, because an opening that balances by accident is not balanced at all.

slides.title: The five checks before you let anyone transact
bullets: Assets equal liabilities plus equity, and the trial balance proves it
Party balances must equal their control accounts, or ageing is wrong from day one
Stock quantity and value must match the count sheet, not the old system's report
The opening journal must be the last document dated before go-live
slides.notes: Two numbers to say out loud in the sign-off meeting: ninety six thousand two hundred ninety of assets, and the same figure on the other side. If the difference is not zero, do not open the doors, because every later correction will be harder once documents exist. This is the moment to be slow rather than helpful.

slides.title: Migration order and what depends on what
bullets: Each row depends on the rows above it, which is why the order is not negotiable
Opening balances come last, because they reference every master
Users and permissions usually precede training, not go-live
Every step leaves an artefact, and the artefacts become the client's audit file

rows: Chart of accounts and cost centres

slides.notes: Print this order and stick it on the wall of the project room, because every delay in a migration traces to somebody working out of sequence. When the client asks to import invoices before opening balances, this table is the answer that ends the conversation politely.

slides.title: What makes an opening balance auditable
bullets: The auditor wants a source document for every opening figure
The count sheet supports stock, the ageing report supports debtors and creditors
The bank statement supports cash, and the fixed asset register supports assets
The equity figure is the only one that is derived, and it must be explained in words

rows: Ageing report from the old system

slides.notes: Every row here has a paper source except equity, and that is the row to explain in the file note. When the audit comes, the client produces this page rather than reconstructing a number from memory. A consultant who builds the evidence table at migration time is remembered as the one who made the audit easy.

lab.title: Lab · Map, import, load the opening and prove it balances
steps: Create the mapping workbook with old and new columns for accounts, parties and items
Confirm every old account has a target and no exceptions remain
Import item groups, then items, then customers, suppliers and price lists
Check each import log for errors and spot-check three item records
Post the stock opening of 47 units at 120.00 through stock reconciliation
Load debtors 13,200.00, creditors 1,188.00, bank 18,450.00 and fixed assets 59,000.00
Balance the opening with equity and confirm the journal difference is 0.00
Print the opening trial balance and confirm assets equal liabilities plus equity
lab.done: Done when the opening trial balance shows 96,290.00 on both sides, party balances equal their control accounts, and the evidence table is complete for every opening figure.

quiz.question: Why must masters be imported in dependency order?
options: Because children reference parents like item groups and territories
quiz.why: ERPNext links records, so an item needs its group and a customer needs its territory before either can be created.

quiz.question: How should stock opening balances be loaded?
options: A journal to the stock account
quiz.why: Stock reconciliation sets both quantity and valuation, whereas a journal would create value with no quantity behind it.

quiz.question: Opening assets of 96,290.00 with liabilities of 3,068.00 require equity of what?
quiz.why: Assets equal liabilities plus equity, so equity is 96,290.00 − 3,068.00 = 93,222.00.

quiz.question: What evidence supports the debtors opening balance?
options: The ageing report from the old system
quiz.why: Debtors are supported by an ageing report or customer statements, while stock uses the count sheet and cash uses the bank statement.

quiz.question: An opening journal shows a difference of 250.00. What should happen?
options: Post it to a suspense account
Stop and find the cause before go-live
quiz.why: An opening that does not balance will corrupt every later comparison, and a suspense account merely moves the problem into a new line.

narration: Migration is where a project is won or lost, and it starts on paper. A mapping workbook with old values, new values and a named owner for every exception is the document the client signs, and it is what ends arguments in month two. Import in dependency order: company, chart of accounts, warehouses and groups, then items, parties and price lists, then users, and only then opening balances. The opening is a journal dated the day before go-live plus a stock reconciliation, and it must balance: ninety six thousand two hundred ninety of assets against three thousand and sixty eight of liabilities and ninety three thousand two hundred twenty two of equity. If it does not balance, the doors stay closed, because every later correction is harder once documents exist. Map on paper, import in order, prove the opening, and only then open the doors to users, with the evidence table signed so the first audit is a page rather than a reconstruction.
